rubrics.justification: The morphology description is detailed and broadly consistent with the provided 3AB grading, including expanded blastocyst, strong ICM, and somewhat looser TE. However, it includes some image-specific claims such as exact ICM position and distinct cellular boundaries that may be more precise than can be reliably supported.
The response thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometriosis, semen quality, endometrial thickness, first-cycle status, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear link from morphology and patient factors to prognosis. Minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments and strong emphasis on stress/endometriosis effects without staging details.

Most recommendations are consistent with standard IVF practice, especially SET and general prognosis framing. However, suggestions such as routine consideration of PGT-A at age 31, ERA, immune modulation, and acupuncture go beyond guideline-supported standard care and are more controversial.

The response gives clear practical next steps for transfer management and future planning, including SET, luteal support, and endometriosis-focused considerations. It is useful clinically, though some proposed adjuncts are not standard and would need careful qualification.
